Point number 2 says: "The evacuation shall be carried out in a planned manner, according to prepared plans along routes leading towards Knin, and then through Otric, towards Srb and Lapac." And my question for you, as the author of this document, is: What did you mean by "prepared plans"?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Under the prepared plans, what was envisaged was what we could see in the previous charts when we were discussing the plan of evacuation for Benkovac municipality. I did not go through those plans, but I presumed and I knew that each locale commune, each municipality, and each village had their respective plans. I warned them that they should stick by the plans, and we assigned them directions of movement. In this case, it was Knin Otric, Srb, and Lapac. Srb and Lapac were the locations where they were supposed to be placed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So that was the plan for all for each of the municipalities would be used, but the destination was changed. Have I understood that right?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. This only pertains to the four municipalities. The others had no evacuation plan and no tasks. Save for the four municipalities, no other municipality received such a decision. There were none.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And my question is: So those municipalities were to use their plannings, such as the one we've seen, but rather than to move them to the areas that we seen, for example, in the Benkovac plan, they were supposed to move them to Srb and Lapac?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct for the five municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And in the course of your discussions with members of the Supreme Defence Council, when you were told to draft this decision, did they tell you that people should go to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, the destination was Srb and Lapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And after the decision was signed by President Martic, what you did you do or what were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: One of the persons competent talked to the people from the Ministry of Defence and civil protection. Their representatives were there headed by the head of civil protection, Colonel Babic. At 4.00 p.m., we're in a building adjacent to the hall, and I read out the decision to them. Babic was there; there was a Mr. Kekic, who was in charge of civilian support Northern Dalmatia; there was a Mr. Vujatovic, who was in charge of Knin; and an another dozen or so representatives from civil protection. There was also the chef de cabinet for the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I am sorry. I just to check. The transcript said that that meeting was at 4.00 p.m. I thought that at 4.00 p.m. you were in your offices. Is that the right time?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I misspoke. It was at 6.00 p.m. It is only logical. You can see that there was a 4.45, and then this was at 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could ask the ask the witness to spell the name of the individual in line 10. I don't think the court reporter was able to pick it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think it was Vujatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we clarify that with the witness, because your understanding is important but not decisive.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vujatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let's go back to that meeting at 6.00 p.m. with the civil protection representatives, who else was at that time meeting?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, the person responsible for evacuation, and it was Colonel Babic. He was in charge of civil protection. Then there were his associates from his team; I don't know who they were though. There was a Mr. Kekic, who was in charge of civil protection for Northern Dalmatia; then there was Mr. Drago Vujatovic, who was in charge of civil protection for Knin municipality. I also no the chef de cabinet of the defence minister was there. I don't know his what name is, but he is a professor, in any case. There were some other ministers. I think it's Mr. Drago Kovacovic; then Mr. Slobodan Peric; and I'm certain that the secretary of the government, Mr. Strbac, was there. There were at least five or six journalists because they were usually accompanying me. I read out the decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just before we go there, if I may interrupt you. Were there representatives of the UN there at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I will explain shortly. When I read out the decision and handed it over to Mr. Babic, since he was to implement it, it was no longer under my competent. It was at that point that UN representatives arrived, people from UNPROFOR, all those that I mentioned previously as being present at 10.00. We planned to ask for their assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you planned -- had you called them before to come to this meeting?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I probably did, or one of my associates on my request --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption, Sir --

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: -- and upon commander's approval. I didn't do anything without his approval.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let's go back to this meeting with the UN. What was the discussion between yourself and the other representatives of civil protection and the United Nations forces representatives.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I opened the meeting, and I was in attendance throughout the meeting. I see that the representatives of the civil protection were somewhat confused. It was obvious that they were not very privy to the situation, especially those who came from the various municipalities. They were asking for a lot of fuel and vehicles; whereas, in the end, it turned out that they needed nothing except for some fuel. We arranged there that the UN representatives were supposed to arrive at 8.00 p.m. to give us their answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you P592, which are notes that are in evidence taken by the UN from that meeting. I want it ask you to review this quickly, it's less than a page, and tell the Court if these notes are consistent with what happened at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Everything is correct, save for the penultimate paragraph. It wasn't said that we were to forward information, but that the UN representatives were to arrive at 8.00 p.m. when they would be given information. Unfortunately, they never did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you another -- another summary of that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's D182, and the parties have stipulated that the date on this document is wrong and should be 4 August 1995. This is half a page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Could you please review this summary of the meeting, and tell us if it is consistent with what occurred at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know this gentleman. For a while, he was the personal representative of the UNPROFOR commander in Knin; that is to say, the commander of the Main Staff in Zagreb. He was his representative in Knin for Sector South. I saw him on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to say that in the paragraph where he says that we suggested the following route, that part is incorrect, as from Srb onwards. We only provided the route stated in the decision. I read out the decision in person, in front of some 20 to 30 people, and I did not go any further than Srb and Lapac. As for Bosanski Petrovac, and places mentioned therein, I don't know where that came from. As for the population from Benkovac and Obrovac, going through Pajane rather than Knin, that is correct. That second part of the route is incorrect and that was not discussed. We cannot find it in the documents either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Novakovic. Let me just change topics now for the -- for my last series of questions. And in your latest statement of last month, which is now P1094, you provided detailed information with respect to various buildings in Knin and how they were used. This statement, as you know, is now in evidence, so I won't ask you any questions, for now, on this, although you may have some questions put to you by others. I would like to briefly go through the same exercise for the facilities, the military facilities in Benkovac, as this is the area you're most familiar with. So, first of all, my first question is: Were you aware that there were some barracks used by the ARSK just outside the town of Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, the question assumes he was most familiar. As I know, the foundation here is that he was born in Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think that was already in evidence, so I know the foundation was already there, but I can ask him specifically, if you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, just how he -- it is foundation ... [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That is ... [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, would Benkovac be the municipality at which you would be the most familiar with in the former RSK?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, although I am better acquainted with Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: But outside of Knin, Benkovac would the town and the municipality that you would have the most knowledge on?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question then --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, if we're going to get into military targets, although I understand everyone's home town is near and dear to him, if we could get more foundation on his knowledge of military installations and where it comes from for the town of Benkovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I will ask my questions, and if this is an objection to specific questions, then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think, as a matter of fact, that it is not an objection against specific questions, but to have them preceded by other questions. Perhaps, you could include that in your questions, that what you had awe like to know and on what basis the witness claims he has knowledge of it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, were you aware that there were some barracks used by the ARSK outside of the town of Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was. I knew that at the time when I attended high school; and, of course, as a member of the staff subsequently, I knew where the various barracks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And do you know what was in those barracks on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of August, 1995, in that particular barracks, as in all the other ones, there were predominantly logistic support units. We had the medical corps there, the kitchen complex, the quartermaster`s premises, workshop, clothes-mending workshop, and a technical workshop. I have to say that, in early 1994 and 1993, some elements of UNPROFOR forces were in the barracks as well. I don't know when they left the barracks. However, there were no combat arms present in the barracks --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Combat armed units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: When you say "armed units," are you referring to -- sorry, strike that. Were there were any fighting soldiers, to your knowledge, in those barracks on the 4th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't. Combatant units were all deployed along the engagement line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you D248, which is a map that was prepared by the Defence. I want to ask you whether -- if you can confirm the location of those barracks which is discussed, and it is going to come up in a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It will be page 3 of that document, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you identify for us the location of those barracks on D248?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that; it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just for the record, can you say what it says in writing so that we can have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: It reads "B. Matsura Barracks." That was the Slobodan Macura barracks, and it says "the total service area." That was the area from Benkovac in the direction of Zadar. Although this was part of Benkovac town, it was on the edge of town in the direction of Zadar. It also says, "the forward command post of the 7th Corps," which was never there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's fine. I just wanted you to identify the location of the -- of that. But while you mention it, do you know where the forward command post of the 7th Corps was in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: It did not exist at the time. It came into existence in January 1993 during the aggression on Ravni Kotari, and it was stationed in the village of Biljane. It only existed for a couple of months.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On this map, there is also an indication of a location that is identified as "Dom JNA." Are you aware of such an army hall in Benkovac in August 1995.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. This was within my competence, the army hall. It existed even before -- or rather, it came in existence after World War II, and it was there on the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And how was that used in August 1995?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: In that time-period, a group of wounded persons was put up there because it had a basement, and that particular room had the Red Cross markation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any fighting forces stationed in that army hall?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: We can also see on this map, at the bottom, there is an indications for the command and the communications centres of the 3rd Brigade. Were there such command/communication centres in that approximate location?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is relatively correct. The 3rd Brigade was a small unit; some dozen people in the command. The communication centre was also manned by a couple of people, and they were servicing the units. They may have occupied a couple of homes. Roughly, that's true. That was Sopet [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what about the other indications on the map? There is the -- well, that is in B/C/S. But there is a nun's convent that is identified there. Do you know if that was used at all by the RSK military?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know -- I don't know of the army having used either or any of the religious facilities, be it of Catholic or Orthodox faith. We, as far as I know, didn't have a practice of using them. I don't know if it was just a building or a family home where the convent was housed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what about the a firemen's hall, were you aware of such a facility in Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was on the way out of town on a new road close to the railway station. Organs for civilian early warning was situated -- were situated there, because before the war, it was the civilian protection that had -- or rather, it was only the fireman's brigade before the war which used to have the alarm for early warning, and that was normally where the civilian protection would, if needed, be housed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, was this firemen's hall used by the RSK military?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: What about the hotel that is identified on this map, was that ever used by the RSK military?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: The hotel was largely damaged in 1995. It was not in use. It was empty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: When you there was damage in 1995, was that before Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, definitely before that. Well, damaged in the sense that it was derelict, not that it was destroyed as such. Since it was in disuse, it was in disrepair. That's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And, finally, on this map, the post office of Benkovac, to your knowledge, was that ever used by the RSK military?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: None of the post offices were used. It is possible that certain civilian lines were used, the ones that the command used to have before the war. The army had its own lines and did not use the PTT lines. However, these PTT -- those PTT lines that had been used by the army before the war were probably used by the army also during the war, but not for the purposes of the units themselves, but for the purposes of the commander and several other offices in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: On the 4th of August, did you receive any reports about shelling of the town of Benkovac and what was hit?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not I personally, but the commander would, and he would brief me and others who would go there. We had our operative centre there, and the persons manning it would keep track of the information. We had a great deal of information. Specifically, according to their information, more than 700 projectiles landed in Benkovac. One of my associates was dispatched from Knin to Benkovac to see what the situation was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you receive any information as to what was being targeted or where the shells were following in Benkovac?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: In Benkovac, as well as elsewhere, the rounds were fired indiscriminately. It was scatter-shot fire. We believe that both civilians and military targets were hit. Everything was under fire, just as was the case in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this concludes the Prosecution's examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Misetic, you will be the first to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, you will first be cross-examined by Mr. Misetic. Mr. Misetic is counsel for Mr. Gotovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, first, a little bit of background information about you. You, throughout your time in the so-called Krajina, in addition to being an officer in the RSK army, you were also simultaneously an officer in the Yugoslav People's Army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the same time. When I was Krajina officer, I was only that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... while you're in the Krajina, you were working for the Yugoslav People's Army KOS or, "Kontraobavesajna Sluzba," or the counter-intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, that's not true. I had never worked for KOS. This was precisely the sector that I never quite understood and where nobody ever hired me to work for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if could I have on the screen, please, 1D61-0225, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, as you will see on the screen here, this is letter sent by you to the MUP in Serbia. And in it, you say -- you are requesting approval of citizenship, and you say: "I am an active military officer serving in the Yugoslav People's Army, currently with the post in the Serb Krajina army in the Republic of Serbian Krajina." That is it your signature on the bottom. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, as I said when I started, you were, in fact, an active JNA officer, or Yugoslavia army officer, while you were in the RSK army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, one can see from the document that that is not quite the case. When we were seeking citizenship, we had to state some sort of an activity. We needed to have citizenship for technical issues. It was connected with personnel issues. At any rate, regardless of the inference you can make for this, while we were officers of the RSK, we were not members of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying, because it was on that basis that the issue of citizenship had to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think Mr. Misetic is listening to the original, so could have a pause because now we are loosing the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, if you look at a transcript, page 57, line 7, you'll see that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we do not know what you asked the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask, Mr. Registrar, if we could give Mr. Novakovic a hard copy of another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Misetic, just for --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: To tender this, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- our information, any date known of this document of which the witness says, or could you ask him when he --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When -- you heard the question of the Presiding Judge. When did you send this to the MUP of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. Possibly in 1993, when we were applying for citizenship. I wish to state, however, that I was granted the citizenship only in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, now I ask for, actually it is in e-court already, 1D61-0342, please -- actually, sorry. I ask that this exhibit be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, document ID number 1D61-0225 becomes Exhibit number D920.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D920 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Registrar, if I could have 1D61-0342 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, this is, again, an undated autobiography signed by you; and at the bottom, you write: "I am now serving in the Serbian army of Krajina Main Staff in Knin, and my permanent address Military Post 4001, Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think, or rather, I don't think, I know that this document bears the same date as the one before. The purpose of this document was solely the issue of citizenship. You know that we, the officers, were registered through the 40th Personnel Sector. That is not a secret at all because it was in this way that we received our pay. We were on the payroll there. This does not change what I said, that when we were in Krajina we were exclusively officers of the RSK army, regardless of what one could infer from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... military post, in fact -- sorry. Was your permanent military post, in fact, 4001, Belgrade, while you were serving in the so-called with RSK army?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I had an identity card, a military ID, with Military Post 9000, Knin. This was the auxiliary post, so to speak. This was the military post of the 40th Personnel Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this exhibit be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D921, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D921 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Novakovic, you just mentioned the 40th Personnel Centre, and I would like to show you via Sanction -- I'd like to show you the indictment that the Office of the Prosecutor filed against Momcilo Perisic before this Tribunal. This is the current indictment in that case. And if we could go to page 12, it says at paragraph 45: "Momcilo Perisic's subordinates, under international law, include those personnel over whom he had a material ability to prevent and punish the commission of crimes. They included, but were not limited to ..." Point A says: "All VJ personnel that were assigned or seconded to the VRS and the SVK via the 30th and 40th Personnel Centres of the VJ General Staff ..." Now, were you, in fact, seconded to the army of the RSK through the 40th Personnel Centre of the Yugoslav General Staff?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: In my personal view, no. I was already down there at the time, and I don't know how the technical issue was processed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In the appendix to the indictment of Momcilo Perisic, your name appears: Assistant Commander For Morale, Legal, and Religious Issues, Colonel Kosta Novakovic. Then it cites the autobiography I just showed you: "Colonel Novakovic stated that he served in the Serbian army of the Krajina Main Staff, and his permanent address was Military Post 4001, Belgrade." As a factual matter, Mr. Novakovic, you were a subordinate of Momcilo Perisic. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: That is not correct. As far as this document is concerned, it is the document that you've just shown to me a moment ago. That's the document that we saw in the Serbian language, my CV. Since this is a pending trial that has not come to an end, I can tell you that it is not true. No one in the 40th Personnel Center -- or rather, no one in the Main Staff of the RSK army was subordinated to General Momcilo Perisic, or the VJ army as such. At no point in time was that the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Registrar, if could I have 1D61-0195 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, you had occasion to travel to peace talks in Geneva in 1993. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I draw your attention to the screen here to one such meeting, where the participants in a meeting in Geneva on military matters are identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could scroll down, please, to the Serbian delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First of all, do you recall this meeting?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do have my notes and I recall all the meets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... are you familiar with all of these individuals? Do you know who they are?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who is Bukovnik Milos Krnjeta?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a colleague of mine who was in our Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who is Slobodan Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic was our interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: When he wasn't a translator, what function did he have in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: He was in the 22nd Kordun unit, or he was the liaison officer there. He was the liaison officer between the UNPROFOR command Sector North and the 22nd Kordun Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Was he also an intelligence officer?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of him being anything other than in an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could please have on the screen 1D41-0149. And before I get an objection on the statements, I have put the matters to Mr. Novakovic that I wish to now to put to him with this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, this is a statement given by Slobodan Lazarevic to the Office of the Prosecutor, which I will now show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go to, please, page --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Actually, without going through all the background in the statement, Mr. Novakovic, Mr. Lazarevic testified that he was an intelligence operative?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And if we could go to page 35 of his statement, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: He was asked by the Prosecution to identify various individuals? If you lock at entry 22, according to Mr. Lazarevic, who was with you in the Geneva delegation, Colonel Kosta Novakovic, he was a KOS official. He went to Knin from the 21st Corps in Topusko, now is working for the VJ at the officer's academy. He was running the with RSK army's information centre in Knin. Now, Mr. Novakovic, Mr. Lazarevic says you were, in fact, working for KOS. Were you, in fact, working for KOS while you were in the RSK?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I had never been a KOS officer, or of the state security or the police, never ever. This is it true. It can be checked in various ways. Now would you please repeat your question, bit by bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I think I have answered my question, Mr. Novakovic. Now, were you aware that the RSK intelligence services repeatedly tried to supply both the ECMM and the UN with misinformation?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't know that and I wasn't required to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, you earlier said that Mr. Novakovic had answered your question. I would like to verify whether that is the case. Mr. Novakovic, Mr. Misetic asked you whether, in fact, you were working for KOS while you were in the RSK, because that's what apparently Mr. Lazarevic says. Then you answered: "First of all, I had never been a KOS officer, or of the state security or the police, never ever. This is true. It can be checked in various ways." Did you ever do anything at the request of KOS? So, irrespective of whether you were an officer where you were formally appointed, did you ever perform anything of which you were aware that you did it for the KOS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, that is beyond any doubt. That would not be characteristic of my views and work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I am reminded that I failed to tender 1D61-0195, which is the list of the participants in the Geneva meeting, and I tender that in evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D922.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D922 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, interpreters working for the UN and ECMM who were Serbs from the so-called Krajina were, in fact, working for the Serbian intelligence services. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that. However, I do know that it was the other way around, that the Croatians who were, working as such, worked for the Croatian agencies. However, I do exclude that possibility fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please focus your answer on the question that was put to you. If at the end of your testimony you think that you should add anything to your answers, then you will have an opportunity to do so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Novakovic, earlier, when you were being questioned by the Prosecution, on a couple of indications, you referred to the fact that in your position, as a result of your position, you had intelligence information, for example, on where HV troops were located, which indicates that you, in fact, were communicating with RSK intelligence organs. Did you ever ask the RSK intelligence organs or come to find out what some of their sources were?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Whatever information was processed by intelligence, they sent to the operational organs. I had access to the documents of the operational organs - that's how I came by that information - supplied to the immediate circle within the command; that is to say, the commander and his assistants.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: But you never got into or received any information in your position as to what methods and sources RSK intelligence agencies had?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. It is possible that I received such -- some information, but not in that way. To be specific, at our briefings, the operational officer in charge would say, "This and that unit of the Croatian army is in that area." I never asked how he knew that, and it was not within my competence to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's go to the 4th. Mr. Novakovic, you say in your statement in 2001 at page 12 and today you repeated it at page 28, line 8 of the transcript, something about if the international community had intervened, then the Croatian offensive would have been halted. Please explain what it is exactly you mean "had the international community intervened." Were you expecting them to intervene?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: We were. First of all, you need to know that we were a protected area of the UN, and the name of UNPROFOR envisaged the existence of such protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have 65 ter 5955 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I'm going to show you is the report on what happened during Operation Storm that was filed by General Mrksic to the chief of the Main Staff of the Yugoslav army on the 26th of August, 1995. Now, first, can you tell me why Mr. Mrksic is filing a report to the chief of the Main Staff of the Yugoslav army about Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I have never seen this report before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, as someone who served in both the Yugoslav army and in the RSK army, do you have any idea why General Mrksic would be reporting to the chief of the Main Staff of the Yugoslav army, after Operation Storm, about what happened in Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it would be wise to ask him that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Is it because he was also simultaneously an Yugoslav officer and a Serb Krajina officer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think the witness has already stated he has no knowledge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, he said -- as a matter of fact, I was about to ask him to refrain from giving directions to whom to put questions. You're invited to tell us, Mr. Novakovic, whether you had any idea. If you have please tell us, if you don't have, tell us as well. But whether or not we should put that question to a different person is another matter, which the parties will consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There is also a mischaracterization in the question where he says "... simultaneously an Yugoslav officer and a Serb Krajina officer. " I think the answer of the witness was clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any idea why General Mrksic reported to the chief of the Main Staff of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I truly don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing I can add is that I never submitted any reports to anyone concerning my sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could go to page 28 in the English first, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a 24-page document for this one, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I have 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I have 24, as well, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In e-court, I have got 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, it's numbered page 28 of 29 on the bottom, so that is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which, of course, raises other puzzles: Where are the missing pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you put the questions to the witness, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's page 23, Your Honour, of the English in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I just want it make sure that the Serbian version is also up for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, if you look at the, in your screen, the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And in the English, it is the second paragraph under section 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The army of the Serbian Krajina was and still is considered a part of the VJ, Yugoslav army. It was doing everything it could, but it has remained isolated. We think that the Main Staff of the Yugoslav army should have supported development of the army of the Serbian Krajina in a more courageous and determined way." Now, the army of the Serbian Krajina was, in fact, considered a part of the Yugoslav army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: It needn't be correct what Mr. Mrksic reports, whether it was considered a part of the VJ and whether the VJ actually saw things that way. Mr. Mrksic wrote this some 20 days after the tragic events, and it is questionable what he meant by that. If we thought we were part of the VJ, that doesn't necessarily mean that the VJ shared that view. Wishes of ours are one thing, and the treatment on their part is another, and that can be concluded from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's start there. You say: "If we thought we were part of the VJ, that doesn't necessarily mean that the VJ shared that view." So you thought you were part of the VJ. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: You misunderstand me. I said that if we wished for that, not believed that to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... why did you wish to be part of the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: If the Croatian army had the Croatian Defence Council and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina on their side, it would have been natural for us to have the VJ on ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd of August, or throughout July 1995, how many people, for example, in the civilian and military leadership of the so-called RSK, had a wish to, for example, become part of a Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if we could turn to page 14 of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks as if pages 19 to 23 are missing in the translation, at least in the numbering at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm now told that I'm using the document that was disclosed to us by Office of the OTP, and what was uploaded into e-court by OTP under 65 ter is missing those four pages. So we will obviously add those at the earliest opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Estimate and course of combat activities -- actually, I think we are ing section 4.1, it should be, in the Serbian. Now, it says, and you have mentioned now this, that, internationally, you were waiting for international intervention: "It was foresighted by the plan of defence that the SVK units in the western part of the Republic of Serbian Krajina would carry out combat activities for six to eight days. It was estimated that this would be possible on condition of establishing encirclement and caring of persistent defence. And if you scroll down a few lines, it reads: "It was estimated that within six to eight days, a reaction by international factors, or even probably VRS or VJ intervention, would have occurred."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to page 3 of this document as well, in the paragraph that begins: "The aggression was expected ..." I believe we're not on the right page in the Serbian. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says: "The aggression was expected, and the Main Staff directed the main focus of their work on preparing the units to defend their positions, regions, and areas resolutely for five to civilian days, believing that that would be enough for the international factors and, if necessary, even the Yugoslav army, to react. Certain conditions were established for such a use of the SVK units (ammunition had been secured, small reserves had been established, fortification and obstacles had been created, and the population had been prevented from moving out ...)" Now, Mr. Novakovic, one of the fundamental elements of the plan of the so-called army of Serbian Krajina to defend against the Croatian offensive was to draw in the international community to stop it. Correct? That was a fundamental element of your plan.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why there would have been such a need, since the international community had already participated in the conflict. They offered their assistance in terms of the Vance-Owen Plan until an amicable political solution could be found. That is why there was this presumption that the international community would take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My question is quite specific: Your plan was to hold out for six to eight days and wait or try to get intervention from either the international community, the army of the Republika Srpska, or the Yugoslav army. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, planning is one thing, an implementation is another, as seen here. I didn't see any specific parts of the plan, but I do know that such -- some such elements were contained in the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that this exhibit be marked, and I tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D923.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D923 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, along those lines, Mr. Novakovic, I'd like to show you a video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is 1D61-0247. This is Mr. Martic on the 2nd of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have a similar sound problem as we had before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, what about an early break, so that the matter be resolve during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we resume at 20 minutes to 1.00. Mr. Novakovic, due to these technical problems, the Chamber decides to have a bit earlier as planned our break. We resume at 20 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic have you checked if the problem's been resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: They have been, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it we also know for next time what to do to prevent it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Novakovic, this is a video of Mr. Martic on the 2nd of August on TV Knin. If we could play it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "I surely wouldn't be amongst the living nor with any of you, nor do we have much of a choice; and we are simply destined to win. For this reason, when any state interest is at stake the sole priority should be Defence and on my behalf as the president, I have the support of the Parliament and the government in that the priorities should be the army and defence. Croatia will most likely conduct new aggression towards the Republic of Serbian Krajina. We attempted to delay this by agreements and negotiations in order for it to be avoided. However their position is precisely to gain support for a military solution in order to stabilize themselves within and you know how much instability they're suffering, but if we schedule and I sincerely hope this will be the case, and we wait as a host and defeat them, then our recognition will be truly imminent. The RSK that we then become the utmost reality. It would be realistic that we be recognised world-wide and that Croatia be defeated. They would forced to shake our hands and say the RSK exists."

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Novakovic, you heard Mr. Martic there before the break you said that there indeed were such elements contained in the plan concerning getting the international community involved in preventing the offensive. However, here, I'd like to ask you that was also one of the topics discussed the fact that if the HV launched an offensive and you were able to hold out that that was a means of obtaining international recognition of the Republic of Serbian Krajina, so-called.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I'm not familiar with all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you were a relatively high-ranking individual in the leadership. Were you ever involved in discussions where one of the strategy considers was to in fact as Mr. Martic put it, Wait as a host for the attack, hold off and then by that, invite the international community to recognise the independence of the so-called Republika Srpska Krajina? Were you ever a participant in such discussions?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I attended quite a few meetings. However, this particular one I wouldn't be able to pinpoint who the audience is and where this is. Apparently this was a group of fighters that Martic addressed, and he addressed them. He was extemporizing, it seems to me, and I don't think that he was expressing a political view.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking if you were present at this particular discussion. What I'm saying is were you present for any discussion where that topic was discussed? In other words, using an eventual Croatian offensive as a justification later for international recognition?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything along those lines being specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... into evidence. It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I missed part because of the overlap. Is that the video that is being tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is what I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes Exhibit number D924.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D924 is admitted into evidence. Does that include the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both in English and in the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now I have forgotten to say -- no I said it's admitted into evidence. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, we -- we talking about this international involvement. And let me first call up D327, which is -- actually we don't need the video. You've already testified this morning that you received a phone call or your liaison officer received a phone call before the assault started where you were told by someone in UNCRO or your liaison officer was told by someone at UNCRO that the attack would start at 5.00 a.m. Was your liaison officer an individual by the last name of Kalapac?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mladen Kalapac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned, I believe in your statement, you say that in your 2001 statement at page 9 you describe the source, Mr. Kalapac's source as "a responsible official who requested Mr. Kalapac to convey this information to me," was that responsible information, in fact, Colonel Andrew Leslie?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. He did mention a name, though. He did mention someone I believe to be a person of authority. It is possible, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... on the screen General Leslie's statement via Sanction. Now General Leslie gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor at line 20, he says: "At around 5.30 in the morning I received a phone call in my office from a Captain Karlopac [phoen]... "His first name here it's written, 'Vladen.' I'm sorry, but I don't know how to spell that. Captain Karlopac was a liaison officer located in the ARSK headquarters." Do you know, generally speaking if Colonel Leslie's -- Mr. Karlopac had a good relationship with Colonel Leslie?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: His name is not Karlopac but Karapac, and his first name was Mladen. I'm not aware of what their relations were. I know that professionally they had to with be in touch perhaps as many as ten times a day and this was the case not only with him but with other UNPROFOR officers as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: How many other -- was that the only -- was there one contact that Karlopac received from UN Sector South or were there more before the operation began?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm -- sorry, Your Honour, when I read this, it says that General Leslie received a call from Mr. Karlopac at 5.30, so I just want to make sure -- because I'm getting confused, so I don't want the witness to be confused by the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic when reading this, it is about Mr. Karlopac or Karapac calling Mr. Leslie.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm now referring to the witness's own statement where he says that Mr. Karlopac was called by someone there in UN Sector South.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just take it one step at a time so we can all follow clearly because he just had the statement and on the screen we still have General Leslie's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, will do his utmost best to avoid further confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, you testified that Mr. Karlopac received a telephone call from UN Sector South. My question is was it the only phone call were there one phone call before the operation began, were there multiple phone calls advising the army of the so-called Republika Srpska Krajina that the attack would begin at 5.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I know of the call that I told you about which took place at 4.00 or 4.15, roughly. I can tell you that there was information which perhaps was not verified that some people from the UNPROFOR command in Zagreb called around midnight. I'm not sure whether is this an accurate report or not. I did, however, say that over the last two days, there were many calls, some were benevolent others were malevolent. I know about this one at 4.15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You testified this morning that you were an officer in charge of religious affairs. I think you mentioned the orchestra.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: First of all for information and then for legal and religious affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can you explain where the UNCRO Sector South would contact you. Why were you the person who was contacted at 4.15 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I will have to repeat my function then. I think I said that I in no unclear terms that I was assistant commander for information, legal affairs, religious affairs, and relations or cooperation with international organisations. In other words, my sector was in charge with direct contacts with all representatives of all international organisations; namely, UNPROFOR, Red Cross, the High Commission, and all the other international organisations present in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you find it unusual that the UN Sector South was giving you information in advance about a military operation that was about to commence at 5.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, as you've just said, you are the officer in charge of liaising with the international organisations. Do you consider it a violation of UN neutrality for the UN to advise one party in the conflict that the party is about to launch an operation against it?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Why would that be the case? Well, if we are now unfolding the story, we should go back to 1st May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, you had --

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Didn't UNPROFOR receive information from the Croatian side that the Croatian side would launch an attack?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, they shouldn't have done so. If the Croatian side had informed them about it, then they should have passed the information on. The UNPROFOR didn't have to be neutral. Why would UNPROFOR protect any side? Why don't you interpret for yourself the very title of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... UNCRO at the time. But putting that aside, okay?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: UNCRO, you understand, was not allowed to take sides in the conflict. You understand that principle. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, the fact that you were able to receive this information from UNCRO in advance was something that was a result of the fact that you had developed good relations with some of the UNCRO officers in Sector South. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that's the reason why. There's another reason, and if you will allow me, I will explain. After all, I am familiar with this because I followed this issue. UNCRO did have a guilty conscience over events that unfolded in Western Slavonia, and they did want to take some of that guilt burden off their shoulders. However, even many of the Croatian sources revealed that through interception the intelligence structures were able to learn that an attack was imminent. This was not a surprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Follow on that, earlier you established that part of the plan, indeed, involvement of the international -- the international community. I'd like it show you now Exhibit D389, please, talking about intelligence information again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for your information, there is a correction that has been made, and we forwarded to our colleagues in the OTP, in the English translation of this document. We would ask permission to upload the corrected version which is not yet in e-court. But I will take him through it, and I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me show you, Mr. Novakovic. This is an intelligence report from Colonel Mihajl Knezovic, on the 4th of August, talking about the HV artillery assault. If you look at the fourth paragraph, when it talks about what was hit and the amount of rounds, it says: "By the time this information was drafted," which is sometime after 10.00 a.m. on the 4th, and you know that because the paragraph beneath, it talks about, "at 1000 hours," something happened.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It says: "By the time that information was drafted, between 200 and 300 rounds ever different calibres impacted on the town. The first strike was carried out on the building of the SVK General Staff, which suffered great material damage, with the fleet of vehicles almost completely destroyed. Later, the fire was transferred on the military barracks 1300 Kaplara ." And that is the northern barracks, correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the name of the barracks. That was probably its proper name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "The railway intersection," and here is where the translation error takes place. In the original, it says, "... and residential buildings in the area beneath the Knin fortress," not residential buildings "and" the area beneath the Knin fortress. Now, you've just told us that you would receive intelligence information. Did you receive this intelligence report as -- as part of your job to liaise with UNCRO Sector South, did you receive this intelligence report from Colonel Knezovic?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I have never seen the information before. I was in a separate building, and up until the 4th, I was exclusively in contact with the commander and the individuals who came to see me. I wasn't in touch with other commanders or assistants. Every one of the assistants, for instance, Mr. Knezovic, was in charge of intelligence. They were each in charge of their areas of work. I can see that this was his own personal assessment that fire could not be opened from the Livran [phoen] plateau. Well, at any rate, he had information that he received. I received information from my commander who used other sources. My source of information were also people who came to see me and who were went about town. I had my collaborators, if you will, in town, who produced a recording. I don't know that I had this piece of information, but this is common knowledge. I was aware of this information through my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So you were aware of this information through General Mrksic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't say this in so many words, but he conveyed to me the gist of it. He didn't tell me that it was Knezovic, but when I came to see him, he told me what this was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Concerning what was happening in the town of Knin, give me names of people who were giving you information about what was happening in the town of Knin. You mentioned your associates or assistants, but give me names. Who?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, primarily the commander. One of the men was Tihomir Vlaonja. He was my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Up there, there was another man, Trgovcevic, who was chief of the division for the cooperation with international organisations, Mr. Milan Trgovcevic. He was formerly a military attache. The others were not there, but quite a few journalists came, as did people from other structure: Mr. Babic, whom I mentioned, from the Ministry of Defence --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask another question. By 8.00 a.m., by 8.00 a.m., who were your sources about what was happening in Knin?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: My personal knowledge, my personal observations, and the sources from the commander and our operation centre, as well as from my associates. How shall I explain this? I was an open-type structure. One could freely access the office where I was. Journalists would drop by, as well as people who observed things happening in Knin. As for the information concerning units, I could receive that from my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What kind of information could you be getting from units in Knin? Were there units in Knin that were providing information to General Mrksic?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no, not in Knin. The nearest command was perhaps some ten kilometres away from Knin. There weren't any units in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So there are no units in Knin. So General Mrksic presumably then, according to you, is not receiving intelligence about what is happening in Knin from units that aren't in Knin, obviously. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. Units never did provide that sort of information. There was no reason for units to be in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, this report from the intelligence department, you see, doesn't mention, for example, the hospital has been shelled. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Other than some residential buildings in the area beneath the Knin fortress, it doesn't mention shelling of other residential areas in other parts of town. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this isn't what this particular individual said, but others did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: In terms of the intelligence assessment of your own army, there was nothing in the intelligence report that said that there was shelling of residential areas, other than a reference to residential buildings in the area beneath the Knin fortress. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, depending on the time when he wrote this. I can't see the exact time when he wrote the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just wondered on the question that "of your own army," if it is of this report from the army, that question is correct. But now he is expanding the question based on just this document. We don't know whether there were other reports or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think, as a matter of fact, the matter is clear. That's what the witness said. He, more or less, said, Yes, we do not find this in this report. Even if he would have said otherwise, the Chamber is able to read a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... establish that with him, because --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, let me turn your attention, Mr. Novakovic, to D331.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. May I give a comment on this document, if you wish me to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you to do it. If at the end you would like to add anything, please do so; but listen to the next question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, in D311, the original is in French; however, if we could have the English and the B/C/S on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is the UN archives, Mr. Novakovic, and it`s a notation of a conversation you had by telephone with General Janvier on the morning of the 4th, where you were conveying a message from General Mrksic. And if you look, you say, in paragraph 5, you told General Janvier: "They targeted the immediate vicinity of the UNPROFOR Sector South command using direct fire. "They also targeted the hospital and other similar buildings, firing randomly and without any order. UNPROFOR officers located there can confirm these claims." What was your basis on the morning of the 4th, given the intelligence assessment looked at on the screen, what was your basis for telling General Janvier that the HV was targeting the hospital.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: The intelligence was certainly not the main source. I said, at the beginning, that shelling was random and that was the impression we had, and we believed that UNPROFOR shared that impression. Several hundred shells landed in a very short span of time, and this was the communication which took place after 5.00. That was our impression, Mrksic conveyed it to me, I was probably with him at that time, and we passed this information on to General Janvier. We addressed their command because we trusted that they would check this through General Forand. If I had possibly made a mistake, he could have checked that through his commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, first, let's take this step by step. What was the specific piece of information that was the basis of the claim that the hospital was being targeted? Who is the person who witnessed this?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, our units that he were closest to Knin, I said that there were some ten kilometres away, they followed the developments through radar and their stations. All the officers who were billeted chose to the command who were housed in the old people's home could notice that, as well as those who resided close to the Knin fortress. Knin is a small town, three by two or three by three kilometres, and one could observe the events from the slopes and from where the area where the fortress is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You were, in fact, giving misinformation to General Janvier as part of plan to draw in the international community. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can we just ask again Mr. Misetic to make a pause, because I'm hearing the overlap as well in between the translations, and it is it hard to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm following the transcript, Your Honour, so I'm trying to monitor my speed by following the court reporter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question, nevertheless.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, I'm going to put it to you that you, in fact, were providing misinformation to General Janvier in an effort to draw in the international community, to stop the HV offence which was, as you testified earlier, an element of the defence plan. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. This is an untrue assertion. General Janvier did not have to trust us fully. He had his organs out in the field who could confirm that. There was the UN Sector South command there. They were on an elevation and were -- had a clear vantage point to allow them to have all the information, to see all the shells. They had all the instruments and mechanisms necessary for that. We didn't even have to give any information to General Janvier since he had a subordinate general who could always check the information without any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Those were our impressions, that was our view of the situation, but they had the person number two there as a sort of supervisor who could check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Precisely. This is precisely the area that I want to go into next, Mr. Novakovic, because General Forand, in fact, at least from the evidence in the file thus far, reported nothing to the UNCRO or UNPROFOR command in Zagreb about shelling of civilian areas prior to a meeting with you at 10.00 a.m. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is whether the witness is aware of it, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, I'm more worried about the misrepresentation. I can check, but isn't there a letter sent in the morning of the 5th about --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: No. Your Honours, we went through this with General Forand. The first UN --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I will wait for Mr. Russo. Let me continue. Mr. Russo I think has to hear me. Before 1.00 p.m. on the 4th, there is no UN sitrep mentioning shelling of civilian areas, and the issue of the letter to General Gotovina being written was extensively dealt with the examination of General Forand who said it was certainly after 10.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was awareness of the witness. Let's hear his answer. Perhaps you'd repeat the question, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, prior to your meeting at 10.00 a.m. with General Forand, UN Sector South headquarters had not reported up its chain of command that there was any shelling of civilian areas in Knin. Were you aware of that at the time that you had the meeting at 10.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think it was so. When General Forand came, he said that this was not fair and he knew for certain that civilian targets were being hit. Since I did a lot of research, I also read some material containing Mr. Forand's lecture to some Canadian officers in October 1995. General Forand described precisely what took place. He lectured a group of Canadian officers upon his return to Canada in October 1995. He mentions precisely the shelling of civilian targets, and, to conclude, he could also see it with his own eyes, as did his representatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: How did you get into possession of General Forand's assessment?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. In any case, I had an opportunity to read it. I read it in Knin. I don't know how I got it. I had a version in English and in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... General Forand's materials, but you have no idea where you got these materials from?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, in your statement, in 2001, you said, at page 9, that General Forand undertook to do everything in his power to stop the targeting of civilian areas. Then today, at page 32, lines 8 to 10, you said that General Forand promised to intervene through the UNPROFOR or command in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: It is correct that he promised that he would intervene. It may have been my impression that he did. In any case, that what he had promised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... after his promise to intervene, are you aware of what steps General Forand took, but to "intervene with the UNPROFOR command in Zagreb"?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, you seem to have some materials from General Forand. Are you aware of a letter that General Forand allegedly sent to General Gotovina on the 4th?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not. I have not seen or heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, when you say that General Forand promised to intervene at this meeting at 10.00 a.m., did he tell you that he had already intervened before 10.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. He did not come out with such information. He acted in accordance with his position and principles and provided no information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... statement at page 9, you say: "After that meeting, I proceeded to the Knin hospital in an UN APC." Why did you go in an UN APC to the Knin hospital?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: There was no other way. I don't remember that particular detail, whether I asked to go or whether someone from UNPROFOR suggested that, when General Forand was coming. In the personnel carrier, it was Colonel Ratsouk and -- in any case, the crew was two officers and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Why were you going? Why did you go with these UN personnel?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: We wanted to see what the situation was and what UNPROFOR could do to assist the wounded. Electricity was out and there were numerous other problems. We already had information that the hospital had been hit, as, indeed, it was, although I don't know at what point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... who else?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Two officers and two soldiers were there. I don't know whether they came from the French or Canadian contingent; but in any case, there was UNPROFOR APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Did you also at this meeting with General Forand get his agreement to use an UN APC to film the damage that was being caused to the town?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it could have been done by anyone else, except for General Forand. In any case, it seems that somebody needed to go to the hospital, and there was a suggestion made that I board the APC. It probably went via the General.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: You know what Zastava Films is. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's a military/JNA film production company. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: It is a production company which, for the most part, produced educational-material films and short features, and perhaps can I explain in detail further.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's owned by the military. Correct? It was in 1995, let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
