utterances.text: It was always a half-military/half civilian entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, on the 4th of August, did Zastava Film get to use an UN APC to film in the town?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. They filmed without an APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Novakovic, turning your attention now to the evacuation order. I'd like to play for you D326, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "on a large scale, at approximately 5.00 on the 4th of August, 1995, representatives of the civilian authorities gathered at Matic's office. Matic was in uniform, and there was an ashtray and several packs of cigarettes in front of him. We exchanged our helloes. And on the topic of the events, he decided he wanted to evacuate the city, and we should take steps to relocate the civilian population; I must stress the civilian from Northern Dalmatia, meaning from the municipalities of Benkovac, Obrovac, Knin, and Drnis, and from the municipality of Gracac and Lika. "This did not come as a shock to me. I perceived this to be some of a rationale measure. At that moment we passed the order, Kosta Novakovic specifically passed the order. It was then that when we wrote in the order that to protect the civilian population that they take the correction of Knin, Otric, Srb, or Lapac, which are the areas to which the people to be relocated. "It is then Mrksic said, 'What do you mean Srb? We need to go further than that, towards Petrovac and Banja Luka.' Then he cautioned us, that if the civilians embarked on leaving, that the military lines would be at risk. He said, 'If the civilians start, the army will go after them to evacuate them, and we're going have big problems.' "However, sometime during the evening, when he arrived, Mrksic was somewhere on the upper floor. He told me, on the staircase, that the evacuation of the population been ordered. I told him, 'General, the army will fall apart. What do you mean by evacuating the people by this in means of an order.' He said, "This is not in our hands. It was the Supreme Defence Council that decided.' "Then someone had requested Martic, or it was Martic trying to talk to Slobo, but, rather, he spoke with Brane Cmcevic. He got hold of Brano Cmcevic who assured him that -- well, he probably couldn't get a hold of Slobo, and that's why he spoke to Brane. He said no steps would be taken, but Slobo would do nothing. Then for the first time, I heard that it was Martic cursing Slobo."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was waiting for the last line to be translated, which I saw as well, but it seems to not be vital one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Novakovic, you say Drago Kovacevic saying on that say that, in fact, although what was written in the order was to go to Srb, what, in fact, said at the meeting was go to further to Petrovac and Banja Luka. That is, in fact, what happened at that meeting, isn't it, Mr. Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I did not hear that. I don't think that can been at face value. Drago Kovacevic wrote a book in which he states that there were some others present, although I know there were known, because I was in the office before he came. I know him well, and it doesn't necessarily mean that what he says is correct. I can guarantee that there was no discussion beyond what we had agreed on. Mrksic even stressed that since the Main Staff was to be relocated to Srb, we were supposed to make decisions on what to do with the population there and then. There was another meeting which was at 8.30 in the afternoon -- in the evening, when tasks were being issued to the military, and there was no mention of the population being moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: We'll follow on that, Mr. Novakovic. But, first, if we could go back to D923, please, page 13 in the B/C/S, and page 21 in the English, please. This is again General Mrksic's report from the 26th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: If we could go towards the middle of the page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, General Mrksic writes: "The evacuation could not be prevented and stopped with any authorities or commanding measures. After the fall of Western Slavonia, there were many accusations at the expense of the authority, the president of the republic, because the evacuation was not ordered earlier." Mr. Novakovic, on the afternoon of the 4th, isn't it true that at the meetings you attended, one of the concerns was that you did not want to be accused, as the leadership had been accused in Western Slavonia, of not ordering the evacuation fast enough?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. There was no discussion about that, at all. The evacuation followed subsequently for the reasons I have explained. In particular, because, by that time, a part of the civilian population had been on the move, and some ordered needed to be introduced in the evacuation process. I already said that at 8.00 in the morning, the people started moving from the country to the city. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: -- by -- the entire municipality of Plaski was evacuated by that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, could you please avoid overlaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm between a -- well, how to express it. I want to make sure that we stay focussed on the question and answer while I'm also have this dilemma about the translation, but I'm only intervening in an effort to keep us moving forward. If we could go to Exhibit D337, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: First of all, this is, as you can see, Mr. Novakovic, a report from Mr. Akashi to Mr. Annan on the 4th of August in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And paragraph 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, here the report is that -- you have -- "there has been a request from the Knin leadership to evacuate approximately 32.000 civilians from Benkovac, Obrovac, Gracac, and Knin to Petrovac and Banja Luka in Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, let me -- in an effort to speed this up, I won't show you again, Mr. Hedaraly showed you Mr. Ratsouk's report from the same day where he mentions that you had told him that the final destinations were Petrovac and Banja Luka. You mentioned this morning Drago Vujatovic was present with you at this meeting with General Forand. And you recall that Drago Vujatovic was the head of the civil protection for the municipality of Knin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, if I could have on the screen, please, 1D61-0051.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Vujatovic's statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, Mr. Novakovic. And if we could go to page 6 in the English, which is paragraph 28. It's page 8 in the B/C/S. At paragraph 28, Mr. Novakovic, here's what Mr. Vujatovic told the Office of the Prosecutor: "At around 5.00 p.m., I was called to a meeting by Kosta Novakovic by phone at the army hall in Knin." He then mentioned some of the other individuals who you've identified. And says the commander of Sector -- UN forces Sector South and his two associates were also there. Towards the middle of the paragraph, it says: "Then Novakovic read out an evacuation order that he stated was signed by Milan Martic. I recall that Novakovic then dictated to me, and I refer to my notes here from the time, the routes of evacuation for the population. Padjene would be the collection point, the first place where everyone should go, and then wait for instructions there. Next point was Srb, and from then he population was to proceed to Martin Brod. The town of Drvar in Bosnia was to be avoided at all costs because it was being shelled. From there, the" --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: On to page 9, please, in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: "From there, the population was to go to Doljani, Petrovac, and finally Banja Luka, which was the final destination." Mr. Novakovic, this is an official of the so-called RSK who has told the Office of the Prosecutor that it was you who dictated the evacuation route, and it was you who said that the final destinations were Doljani, Petrovac, and Banja Luka. Now, isn't it true that at this meeting you told the UN and your fellow associates at the meeting that the evacuation was to be carried out, to go to Padjene, Srb, Martin Brod, Doljani, Petrovac and Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: That is absolutely incorrect. I never mentioned Padjene. That was not within my purview. I only read out the decision. That was the scope of my limitations there. I read it out. I was not personally interested in Drago Vujatovic because he was a municipal representative. Mr. Babic and his associates were of importance to me, because they were supposed to take it over. I wasn't tasked with passing down the tasks to the lower levels. I read out the decision, and I said that there were 15 to 20 people there. I only read out the text of the decision without any comment, and I said who signed it. Not only did I read it but I held it out and people could come and see it for themselves. There was no mention of any other routes. As to how it was later implemented by certain other individuals, that's another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Well, now let's ask the factual matter -- what actually transpired after this. It turns out that the people actually -- the civilian population did go to Srb, and from there to Martin Brod, and from there to Petrovac, and then to Banja Luka, right? That is actually what did take place.

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: So let me make sure that you have been given every opportunity, Mr. Novakovic. In addition to the fact that it turns out that the people actually travelled this route, it is your position that the UN that attended the meeting is wrong when it says that you said that the final destination was Petrovac and Banja Luka and your fellow associate who was with you at the meeting also got it wrong when he says that you said to go to Petrovac and Banja Luka. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: I claim that, and I say that it is completely incorrect. There were other 10 to 15 people in attendance there who could confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Mr. Novakovic, is it -- is it the case that you do not wish to acknowledge your role in evacuating the population to Petrovac and Banja Luka for fear of being held responsible by your fellow Serbs for ordering the evacuation out of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KOSTA NOVAKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I believe that question is superfluous and it can certainly be disputed by at least another 30 sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer is no. Your point is clear, Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the Trial Chamber's rulings on issues like this, we will not tender this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock. I don't know what your next subject would be, whether that could be dealt with in a couple of minutes. If so, please proceed; if not --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I don't wish to run afoul ^ with the Trial Chamber so I will not risk it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes, apart from that, I get problems with the other Trial Chambers. Mr. Novakovic, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning. Madam Usher, can you escort Mr. Novakovic out of the courtroom. And I would like to instruct you before you leave this courtroom that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether it is the testimony you have already given or whether the testimony still to be given from now on. Is that clear, Mr. Novakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which leaves one minute to inquire with the parties, whether the indicated time need, and in view of how the cross-examination develops is still accurate, or whether it undergoes any changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will -- I anticipate and I'll tell you what the issue is. There were several people on the Prosecution's witness list including -- well, I don't mention the names but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You explained that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... directly involved, for example, the entire structure of the civil protection, how orders were carried out. This is my only opportunity to -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... just asking --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether your original estimate is still the same, whether it became --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It became a little less. I won't take ten hours, but I certainly will take all of tomorrow and try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. That's clear. That's just for our -- for everyone, good to know that if there is any adjustment to estimates that we are aware of that. We adjourn, and we resume tomorrow, Friday, 14th day of November, 9.00 in the morning, in this same Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 14th day of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
